transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-11-29
Start: 15:30 PST
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Jordan Lee (Redwood SE), Rachel Chen (PlatinumSearch Head of Search), Devon Miller (Eng Manager), Sofia Alvarez (Data Scientist)
Links shared: deck: https://redwood.app/decks/platinum-plug, benchmark sheet: https://redwood.app/benchmarks/platinum-search.csv, security packet: https://redwood.app/security/platinum

Summary (auto): Quick hosted API demo focusing on embeddings + reranking to improve search relevance; walked through API examples, Console metrics, and Optimize suggestions for cost/latency. Customer concerned about PII/data residency and predictability of latency for 200 RPS peak.

Transcript:
00:00 Samir: hey everyone thanks for joining, i'm Samir from Redwood, i'm joined by Jordan our solutions eng, we're gonna walk through the hosted API embedding and rerank flow, demo the console a little and then talk POC next steps, sound good?
00:12 Rachel: yep that sounds great thanks, um our main goal is improving relevance on product search \u00151 we see a lot of tail queries, and current vector store is okay but rerank would help, also need latency under 200ms p95 ideally.
00:25 Jordan: great \u00151 quick q, when you say current vector store, are you using an external index like pinecone or are you self-hosting?
00:31 Rachel: we are on pinecone for now, plus we have a bespoke BM25 fallback, so hybrid, though pinecone configs are a pain to tune, yes.
00:42 Devon: just to add, our infra is in us-west-2, and we have strict data residency for EU customers but most of our traffic is NA, also SSO via Okta for internal tools.
00:55 Samir: thanks, good context. we'll show embeddings + a lightweight reranker that sits after the vector retrieval; our hosted API handles both pieces \u00151 embeddings endpoint, and then a rerank endpoint that scores candidates using the model. we'll show cost/latency tradeoffs and the optimize suggestions for batching and quant profiles.
01:12 Jordan: jumping in \u00151 here's the typical flow: 1) call embeddings endpoint to index or to encode query, 2) nearest neighbors search in your vector DB, 3) call Redwood reranker with the query + top-k candidates to produce final ordering. We'll demo a quick example with a 256-d embedding and a cross-encoder style rerank.
01:30 Rachel: 256 dims? what about recall vs cost, we were using 768 dims earlier.
01:36 Jordan: yeah so there's always a tradeoff \u00151 higher dims usually help recall for semantic neighbors but larger vectors cost more and increase indexing/IO. Our Optimize tool will suggest a profile based on sample distribution; for your workload with many short product titles 256 or 384 often gets close to 768 with the right reranker.
01:56 Sofia: can you show the API request/response shape? we want to share with our engs.
02:02 Jordan: sure \u00151 here's a snippet (presenting code) \u00151 POST /v1/embeddings body: {"model":"redwood-embed-jan24", "input": ["query text"]} returns embeddings array. Then rerank: POST /v1/rerank {"model":"redwood-rerank-v1","query":"...","candidates":[{"id":"123","text":"...","metadata":{}}]} response includes score and explanation. (note: code in deck)
02:28 Rachel: ok and what are typical latencies? for rerank at top-k=10.
02:33 Jordan: on hosted API we've seen p95 rerank latencies around 70-120ms for cross-encoder style on redwood-rerank-v1 depending on load; embeddings are single-digit ms for small batch sizes. With continuous batching and our kv-cache for conversational contexts it can be even lower.
02:52 Devon: p95 120ms at what RPS? our peak is 200 RPS with spiky traffic.
02:58 Jordan: good q \u00151 those numbers are for moderate load on shared hosted endpoints, at 200 RPS you might want a dedicated pool or to use a hybrid approach: hosted embeddings + dedicated reranker or set autoscaling for Dedicated. For Hosted we offer traffic tiers and regional routing \u00151 we can run a benchmark with your queries to get concrete numbers.
03:20 Rachel: security questions \u00151 we need SOC2, KMS support, and audit logs. also any PII handling for user queries?
03:30 Samir: yes, we are SOC2 Type II, we provide KMS integrations and HSM options for Private deployments, and audit logs are available in Console. For hosted we have encryption at rest and in transit; we also support retention policies and optional redaction in pre-processing. I'll share the security packet after.
03:49 Sofia: quick nit, do you keep any copies of raw queries on hosted? we need to know retention windows.
03:54 Samir: by default short retention for debug logs, but we offer retention controls and enterprise customers can opt out of retention or go to Private (VPC/on-prem) for no copies, we can put that in the docs.
04:12 Devon: do you support SAML SSO for the Console?
04:15 Samir: yep Okta/SSO via SAML and SCIM for provisioning, RBAC in Console.
04:21 Rachel: can the reranker be customized or fine-tuned? we have a clickstream and relevance labels.
04:27 Jordan: two paths \u00151 you can provide a labeled set and we run offline training to calibrate the reranker (pairwise tuning), or you can do a lightweight prompt+context approach with the reranker model and signal features. We also support feature injection (product metadata) into the reranker request.
04:45 Sofia: what's the pricing model for rerank calls? per-token, per-call, or hybrid?
04:50 Samir: rerank is usually per-inference unit (per-call) with an embedded token cost for large inputs; embeddings are per-embedding unit. We'll send the detailed pricing sheet. For POC we can arrange trial credits.
05:03 Jordan: demo time \u00151 switching to Console \u00151 (screen share) you can see per-route latency, token breakdown, and per-model cost. Here's an Optimize suggestion: for your distribution we recommend enabling small-batch aggregation and using int8 quant profile on rerank to save ~30% cost with minor accuracy regression.
05:30 Rachel: does quantization affect determinism? we need consistent scoring for experiments.
05:34 Jordan: quantization can introduce small variance; we recommend running A/B tests in the Console using rollouts. Redwood has automatic rollback if quality drops beyond threshold.
05:45 Devon: what about retrie- retrieval step, we're still on pinecone \u00151 any preference?
05:50 Samir: no strong preference, we integrate with Pinecone, Weaviate, Milvus, or you can host your own vector store. Many customers keep Pinecone for nearest neighbor and call Redwood rerank after retrieval.
06:05 Rachel: ok show us a live query?
06:10 Jordan: yep pushing a sample query now \u00151 (Jordan types) Query: "wireless noise cancelling earbuds under $100" retrieving top 10 from Pinecone and sending to reranker, results show before and after reordering.
06:28 [screen] Jordan: Before rerank top result A, after rerank top result B (more relevant to price constraint).
06:36 Rachel: nice, i like that the reranker can respect constraints like price or brand when given as metadata.
06:42 Jordan: exactly \u00151 you can inject metadata into candidate objects and we use it as features; plus you can add guardrails like must-have attribute filters.
06:54 Devon: any cost estimate for doing rerank at scale, e.g. reranking top 10 at 200RPS?
07:02 Jordan: rough back-of-envelope: if rerank call is ~100ms in hosted and counts as one inference per request, at 200 RPS that's 17k calls per minute; we'd model throughput on a dedicated pool or autoscaled hosted capacity. We'll include a cost model in the pricing spreadsheet. For Dedicated you get committed throughput and lower unit cost.
07:25 Rachel: our key success metric is NDCG@10 improvement of +0.08 over baseline, also keep p95 latency <200ms.
07:32 Samir: noted \u00151 we'll run the POC with those metrics and include NDCG evaluation in the benchmark sheet.
07:38 Sofia: how do we handle user-level PII? we use email fragments in queries sometimes.
07:43 Samir: you can configure pre-ingest redaction and also use client-side hashing; for sensitive workloads Private is recommended. We'll attach the PII handling section of the security doc.
07:55 [small cross talk as Jordan toggles to performance tab]
08:12 Jordan: here are example benchmark results \u00151 small sample: embeddings 5-12ms p95, rerank 85-140ms p95 on hosted; with quant and dedicated this can drop to ~60-90ms. These are with top-k=10 cross-encoder.
08:30 Devon: do you provide tracing for request-level latency breakdown?
08:34 Jordan: yes Console has per-request traces, token-level and stage-level breakdown (embed -> retrieve -> rerank -> postprocess). We can stream logs to your SIEM too.
08:45 Rachel: awesome. question on model versions \u00151 how do rollouts work? can we pin an older model if quality dips?
08:51 Samir: yes, model pinning and gradual rollouts are built-in. You can do canary percentage, and automatic fallback to a pinned model if error rate rises.
09:02 Sofia: any gotchas about cold starts?
09:05 Jordan: cold starts are minimal with our runtime; we also warm pools based on traffic patterns in Console. For strict latency SLOs many customers use Dedicated or reserve burst capacity.
09:18 Devon: what about on-prem or VPC? we might need a Private deployment for certain EU customers.
09:24 Samir: Private is available; it includes a customer-managed control plane, KMS integrations, and audit logs. We'll give the network diagram and packaging options in the security packet.
09:36 Rachel: ok, sounds good. can we run a small POC: hosted embeddings + rerank for 2 weeks with 10k sample queries and measure NDCG and latency?
09:44 Samir: absolutely, that's the typical path. Jordan will own the benchmark and we'll provide a template.
09:50 Jordan: i'll share the template after the call \u00151 it includes data format, expected columns (query, ground_truth_ids, session_id) and scripts to calculate NDCG@10.
10:00 Rachel: perfect. two more quick Qs: do you have SLO-based credits if SLAs missed, and who is the escalation contact?
10:07 Samir: SLA credits are in the enterprise contract, yes; escalation is CSM + on-call infra eng, we'll include contacts in the doc.
10:14 Devon: timeline \u00151 if POC starts 12/8, how long until we get draft pricing and Dedicated estimates?
10:19 Samir: we'll send pricing and Dedicated outline within 3 business days after POC kickoff; draft contract terms in a week.
10:26 Rachel: cool. any blockers from our side? we just need the sample queries and service account creds for ingestion.
10:32 Devon: i'll get the creds and sample queries to Sofia and cc you.
10:36 Sofia: i'll try to deliver 10k queries by 12/06.
10:40 Samir: great \u00151 recap quick: Samir send pricing & security packet; Jordan share benchmark template and scripts; Sofia provide queries; schedule POC start 12/8.
10:52 Rachel: sounds good thanks team.
10:56 Samir: thanks all \u00151 we'll follow up with calendar invite and docs.

End of transcript.

Notes (auto): some transcription artifacts in places (k-v cash -> kv-cache, quan-tization -> quantization). Mentioned integrations: Pinecone, Weaviate, Okta. Action items captured above.
